title: IUPAC Nomenclature Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A home address gives a number, a street and a city. A cinema ticket gives a row and a seat. A chemical name can give the whole drawing of a molecule. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 8, Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques) we learn IUPAC nomenclature of organic compounds.

On the molecule bench we build names part by part: word roots (meth to hex), primary suffixes (ane, ene, yne) and secondary suffixes (ol, al, one). We name 2-methylpentane with the longest chain and lowest locant rules, add di and tri, alphabetical order and cyclo, then name compounds with functional groups link by link, including priority and halogen prefixes. Then propan-2-ol vs propanone, a full worked example, benzene derivatives with ortho, meta and para, the exam trap, an original JEE / NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 81 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Three codes, read in parts
0:35 Prefix, word root and suffixes
1:22 The molecule bench: naming 2-methylpentane
1:59 More rules: di, tri, alphabetical, cyclo
2:20 Functional groups and priority, link by link
2:54 Propan-2-ol vs propanone
3:34 Worked example: 3-methylbutan-1-ol
4:03 Benzene names: ortho, meta, para
4:23 Exam trap: the chain drawn straight
4:49 Practice question (JEE / NEET pattern)
5:22 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Isomerism in Organic Compounds. How can two molecules have the very same formula, yet be different?
